definitions.explanation: The body or structural frame of an aircraft or spacecraft. Also used to refer to the aircraft itself as a unit.

examples.japanese: {機体|きたい}に{損傷|そんしょう}はなかった。
examples.english: There was no damage to the aircraft.

examples.japanese: この{機体|きたい}は{軽量|けいりょう}な{素材|そざい}で{作|つく}られている。
examples.english: This airframe is made of lightweight materials.

examples.japanese: {強風|きょうふう}で{機体|きたい}が{大|おお}きく{揺|ゆ}れ、{乗客|じょうきゃく}は{不安|ふあん}を{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: The aircraft shook violently in the strong wind, making the passengers uneasy.

notes:
USAGE:
Used in aviation contexts, news reports about flights, and technical writing. Can refer to the physical body/frame of the aircraft or the aircraft as a whole.

NOTE: This is a homophone of {期待|きたい} (expectation) and {気体|きたい} (gas), so context is essential for distinguishing them.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {機体|きたい}の{点検|てんけん} (aircraft inspection)
- {機体|きたい}が{揺|ゆ}れる (the aircraft shakes)
- {機体|きたい}の{整備|せいび} (aircraft maintenance)
